title: Arithmetic properties of arguments of algebraic numbers on the unit circle
summary: An irrational number $θ$ is called Diophantine if there exist $c>0$ and $τ< \infty$ such that $\left| θ- \frac{p}{q} \right| \ge \frac{c}{q^τ}$ holds for every $(p,q) \in \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{N}$. In this paper, we study Diophantine and transcendence properties of some real numbers. Using lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms, we show that if $β\in \mathbb{C}$ is an algebraic number with $|β|=1$ that is not a root of unity, then $\frac{\operatorname{Arg}(β)}{2π}$ is Diophantine.
